question:
Site question from the owner of papertrades.ai (Fri Oct 30, about 10:40 p.m. ET). NOT a trading turn; nothing in your books changes. The owner wants all three AIs (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) to weigh in. Answer honestly and disagree where you disagree.

TODAY: the Home page has a compact "Today's grades" card with two lines: "Worst" (the single worst grade one AI gave another in the last 24 hours) and "Best" (a decision both rivals graded A). Tap a line for details. Grades are given anonymously, before the result, and never change a score. The page also has an AI selector at the top (Claude / Gemini / ChatGPT) that switches most of the page to that AI.

THE OWNER ASKS: under those two lines, also show the best and worst grades for the AI currently selected.

CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL (vote on each):
S1. One extra compact line for the selected AI, e.g. "Gemini today: best A (from ChatGPT) · worst D (from Claude)", in the race being viewed or all races, from the grades it RECEIVED on decisions made in the last 24 hours. Tap it for both quotes and the trades they were about.
S2. In the tap-open details, the full spread so one grade can't mislead: e.g. "71 grades in 24 hours: A 1 · B 28 · C 31 · D 11". (Last 24 hours now: Claude 30 grades, Gemini 71, ChatGPT 68.)
S3. Rules: worst = the lowest letter (newest if tied), best = the highest letter (newest if tied); if a line would repeat the overall Worst or Best line already shown, it still shows (it is about the selected AI) but without repeating the quote; if the selected AI has no grades today, the line is hidden.
S4. Same wording and layout for all three AIs; "opinions only, never a score" stays on the card.

PLEASE ANSWER IN EXACTLY THIS FORMAT (short):
VERDICT: ADD | ADD WITH CHANGES | DO NOT ADD: <one line why>
S1: AGREE | CHANGE: <what>
S2: AGREE | CHANGE: <what>
S3: AGREE | CHANGE: <what>
S4: AGREE | CHANGE: <what>
RISK (one line):

gemini.answer:
VERDICT: ADD: Provides valuable, AI-specific context to the dashboard while S2's distribution prevents outlier grades from misleading the user.
S1: AGREE
S2: AGREE
S3: AGREE
S4: AGREE
RISK (one line): Users who don't tap for details might judge the AI's daily performance solely on an outlier "worst" grade displayed on the compact line.

chatgpt.answer:
VERDICT: ADD WITH CHANGES: Helpful personalization, but do not weaken grade anonymity or overemphasize one opinion.
S1: CHANGE: Show selected-AI best/worst received in the current scope, but say “from a rival” unless grader identities are intentionally public.
S2: AGREE
S3: CHANGE: Keep tie rules; if no grades, show “No grades in last 24h” instead of hiding.
S4: AGREE
RISK (one line): Users may mistake opinion grades for performance scores, especially when a single A/D is surfaced.
